_comment: Ordered text substitutions applied to the FINAL assembled prompt, right
before it is sent to the model. The usual reason to want one is a person
the bot keeps addressing by their Discord username or their decorative
display name rather than by the name you want the model to use.
Rules run in the order listed, each on the output of the one before it, so
a later rule can act on an earlier rule's output. Order is therefore
load-bearing — reordering these rules can change the result.
SCOPE: these rewrite the outbound API call ONLY. Stored conversation
history, the database and the dashboard activity log all keep the original
text, so the logs stay a truthful record of what was actually said.
FIELDS
match         (required) literal substring, or a raw pattern if regex:true
replace       (required) replacement text; "" deletes the match
regex         (optional) false = literal (default), true = real regex
caseSensitive (optional) false = ignore case (default), true = exact case
enabled       (optional) false = skip this rule without deleting it
MATCHING RULES (the subtle part)
A literal rule matches whole words only, so "Critter" will not fire
inside "Critters" or "Supercritter". The boundary is an explicit
lookaround on word characters rather than \b, because \b is defined
against [A-Za-z0-9_] and therefore cannot match around a name that starts
with a decorative symbol such as the one below.
"dumb.critter"  in  "dumb.critter's"   ->  "Critter's"   (possessive kept)
"dumb.critter"  in  "dumb.critters"    ->  unchanged      (plural s blocks)
"dumb.critter"  in  "xdumb.critter"    ->  unchanged      (leading x blocks)
The possessive is deliberately allowed and the plural deliberately is not.
Rewriting "critters" would yield "Critics", silently turning a person's
nickname into an insult, unattended, in every message. A rule that misses a
word is recoverable; one that corrupts one is not. If you WANT the plural
rewritten too, add a separate rule for it.
LITERAL MODE IS NOT REGEX MODE
In the default literal mode the '.' in "dumb.critter" matches a literal
dot, not any character, and a replacement containing $& or $1 is inserted
verbatim rather than expanded. Set "regex": true to opt into a raw
pattern; a regex rule gets no automatic word boundaries, so it must
anchor itself if it needs them.
This file is hot-reloadable and can be overridden per profile at
prompt_storage/profiles/<id>/config/rewrites.json.
